recipes.name: Mrs. Sigg's Fresh Pumpkin Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 recipe pastry for a 9 inch single crust pie

steps.text: Cut pumpkin in half and remove seeds. Place cut side down on a cookie sheet lined with lightly oiled aluminum foil. Bake at 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) for 30 to 40 minutes, or until the flesh is tender when poked with a fork. Cool until just warm. Scrape the pumpkin flesh from the peel. Either mash, or puree in small batches in a blender. Increase oven temperature to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C.)
In a large bowl, slightly beat eggs. Add brown sugar, flour, salt, 2 cups of the pumpkin puree, pumpkin pie spice, and evaporated milk. Stir well after each addition.
Pour mixture into the unbaked pastry shell. Place a strip of aluminum foil around the edge of the crust to prevent over browning.

Bake 10 minutes at 450 degrees F (230 degrees C), then reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Bake an additional 40 to 50 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean. Remove the strip of foil about 20 minutes before the pie is done so that the edge of the crust will be a light golden brown. Cool pie, and refrigerate overnight for best flavor.

raw_recipe.headline: Mrs. Sigg's Fresh Pumpkin Pie
raw_recipe.description: A mixture of fresh pumpkin puree, brown sugar, spices, evaporated milk and eggs is poured into a prepared pie crust and baked.

review.reviewBody: Well, I thought I messed up. I baked the pumpkin for an hour, it was tender when I poked it. As I scraped the flesh away from its skin, it was gritty and dry, not mushy or smooth as I thought it would be. I had already mixed the eggs, sugar etc. so I had to give it a try. It poured into the pie crust (two regular sized ones) like water! I was so upset because I was to take it to Thanksgiving dinner the next morning!! It baked up beautifully and not a crumb was left the next day! I'm making another (one deep dish this time) and this time the pumpkin scraped off smooth like it is out of a can, NEVER fear, it will work out no matter the texture of the pumpkin! I used the Best Ever Pie Crust recipe from this site.....it's terrific!!!

This really is a good recipe. I figured a few things out after making this that might help others. 1. Puree the pumpkin in a food processor. If you don't the pie will have a rough texture. 2. Only add 1 c. of evaporated milk. The pie will set better and you will not have too much filling. 3. If you use all brown sugar the pie will be very brown in color. My family prefers it with half brown and half white sugar. 4. Do not overbake!! Check it 10 minutes before it says in the recipe. Mine was done after 40 mins. total bake time. If you overbake the pie, it will taste grainy instead of creamy. Hope these suggestions help!

Good recipe . A "pie gourmet" neighbor rated it a 8.5/10 ! I made a few amendments. Substituted condensed milk for evaporated, omitted the sugar. (Condensed milk is already sweetened.) I roasted and added two turnips to the pumpkin, added more flavor so spices didn't dominate. I don't know exactly what pumpkin spice is so added, 1 tsp of each cinnamon , nutmeg and allspice. 
Pre-baked 'Mrs. Smith's frozen pie crust for 10 min at 450. Followed all other directions as written. YUM,

I used 6 pie pumpkins, which yielded 10 store bought deep dish pies, reduced salt to 1/4 tsp and increased pumpkin pie spice to 1 tbsp per recipe, baked at 450 for 10 minutes, 350 for 25 minutes, no cracks.
I let my puree drain overnight in cheesecloth lined sieves which makes the texture similar to canned pumpkin.
#AllrecipesAllstarsCanada
#PumpkinCraze
Loved this recipe! I cooked my pumpkin in the microwave until soft,then scraped the flesh out. It worked great! I also used 1 tablespoon of pumpkin pie spice. Turned out great! Yummmm....

I loved this recipe. I was concerned about the initial consistency the first time. I put everything in a blender the second time I made it, and it baked fluffier. My pumpkin was watery after draining so I added a tablespoon of flour and took off an 1/8 cup of condensed milk, added 10 mins. Perfect!

You know you've found a good recipe when your husband says "This is the best pumpkin pie I've ever had." I baked the sugar pumpkin ahead of time, so two days later when I actually made the pie, it was so easy. I did as the other reviewers suggested, and used 3 Tbsp. of pumpkin pie spice. I also blended all the ingredients in my Vitamixer (low speed for a minute or so). The results were a smooth, creamy, light consistency. This will definitely be my go to recipe, and I'm no longer afraid to make a pumpkin pie from scratch. I always thought it would be too difficult and too involved. It was pretty easy!! I used a roll-out crust from Whole Foods. Maybe soon I'll venture into making my own pie crust!

Very straight-forward to make, and the result is sublime. When warm, it seems like there's too little spice, but when it's completely cool the amount turns out to be PERFECT.

I used a convection oven, so lowered all the temperatures by 20C (cooking at 210C for 10 minutes, then 155C for 40 minutes). I didn't use aluminium foil and the pastry turned out perfectly, no burning. In the Netherlands, "Spekulaaskruiden" can be substituted for the pumpkin pie spice, and in the UK, "Mixed Spice" (in both cases the taste/ingredients are virtually identical to pumpkin spice).

I have always used canned pumpkin for my pie. But, I grew pumpkins this year, and had 2 beautiful sized ones I didn't know what to do with. I decided to roast the pumpkins and try a 'fresh' pumpkin pie. I am glad I did! This recipe is delicious!!! My son is a pumpkin pie lover.....and he told me this is the best pie he has tasted. Maybe because it is made from home grown pumpkins, but there clearly is a difference in taste between canned pumpkins and home grown, right out of your garden, pumpkins. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe. I didn't adjust ingredients.....perfect as is! I did adjust the baking time. I baked the pie at 350 degrees for 45 minutes in total. I never cooked the pie at 450 for the first 10 minutes, and I did not cover the crust with foil. Didn't need it if you have a good, prepared, hot oven (or in my case, a small countertop oven). Definitely use a food processsor, but start with mixing all of the wet ingredients first, then add the pumpkin and process a bit longer. No grit, no stringy parts....smooth consistency. Beautiful.

I haven't used any other recipe since I've found this one! This year I did make a few changes though and it was even better, not that I thought it was possible, but my family also likes a little more spice. Here's what I did: First of all, my blender wasn't doing what it was supposed to do, so I added all the ingredients at the start with 1/4 -1/2 tsp ground cloves added in and only 3/4 can evaporated milk ...I still had left over filling...Anyway, I blended the ingredients on the lowest speed, gradually increasing till the fastest, blending until I began to see a few bubbles, then poured it into a frozen deep dish pie crust. Saved alot of time and dishes!! A must for anyone who hates the clean up!!!

I just made this for Thanksgiving and it is so delicious! I made a few mini pies for us to try before we take the big one to our family party tomorrow and they were so amazing! The flavor of the pumpkin filling is perfect, not to sweet, and it isn't hard at all to roast the sugar pumpkin. I threw all of the filling ingredients into the blender so it would be super smooth and less clean up. I also only used 3/4 of a can of evaporated milk because some of the reviews said it was too runny and I used 1 TBS Pumpkin Pie Spice just so it would be more flavorful. I used a refridgerated Pillsbury crust, used an egg white wash and blind baked it so it wouldn't get soggy (350 for 10 min then let it cool) and definitely use the foil! There was enough filling for two pies. Thank you for the recipe Beth!
I added an extra tablespoon of flour, and did 1.5 tablespoons of seasonings (mix of nutmeg, ginger, cinnamon and allspice). It was very good with these tweaks.
Our absolute favorite way to make homemade pumpkin pie!
This was so easy and a great tasting pumpkin pie recipe. i bake 3 pies and share them with two of my neighbors each thanksgiving.
Was definitely worried with the water.. Took about an hour on my electric oven. Used a Graham cracker crust. I also added 1/2tsp of allspice and clove. Came out really great.

Five years ago I was introduced to a homemade pumpkin pie. I could not believe how different a store bought pie was verses a homemade. After that first taste I went in search of a recipe that I could make from scratch. This was it. I have never looked back and am very thankful for this recipe. I have been asked over and over again to make this homemade pumpkin pie. I won't ever go back to store bought. This is an easy, yummy pie that you cannot beat. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe. Kelly

I am eagerly waiting to taste these pies, I like lots of spice! I doubled the batch and used: 2 1/4 tsp cinnamon 1 1/4 tsp ginger 1/2+ tsp fresh ground cloves 1/4 tsp allspice 1/4+ tsp fresh grated nutmeg I baked 3 sugar pumpkins and got 5.5 cups of puree after straining water out (saved 1.5 for another time). I think I over cooked the pies a bit, but I'm sure will still be delicious.

This pie is amazing and I have made it for Thanksgiving for a few years now! Once you have pie made fresh from a pumpkin, you cannot go back to canned puree ever again. The flavor and texture is on point, and although you may be excited to dig in upon making the pie—it really is best to let it refrigerate overnight for the BEST flavor possible. Will always use this recipe!
I’ve been making this recipe for years and absolutely love it. I find it great as is; however, its a little nicer if you bump up the pumpkin spice to a tablespoon. Great pie! My family loves it.
